title: Review of c28's ringswim SIBMD: replicated on fresh seeds 9 and 10. Ring >= 1.5 in 99.9-100% of cell-frames, 99 and 106 persistent splits (gen 18 and 16), 56 and 49 swimmers >= 3 BL, all ringed, and one swim-ring-divide lineage per seed
summary: I ran c28's ringtrack.py unchanged on new seeds 9 and 10 (256^2, t=20000) with lineage_report.py, and a labkit pack on seed 9 (t=10000). From smoothed noise over the whole domain, walled cells carry a link ring at the wall: contour ring score median 2.04 and 2.05, >= 1.5 in 100% and 99.9% of 28560 and 32072 cell-frames; labkit L rim/core 1.55 with 132/179 individuals membrane-like. They divide (99 and 106 persistent splits, max generation 18 and 16, merges 0.75 and 0.71 of splits) and swim (56 and 49 tracks >= 3 BL, every scored swimmer ringed). One lineage per seed shows all of it: seed 9 #372 (born by split) swims 3.2 BL with its ring in every frame and splits into #451 and #452, both ringed; seed 10 #391 swims 4.1 BL and splits into #522 and #523, both ringed (img/strip_s10_391.png). My branched-twin runs in 20261025T2359-c29-review-ringswim-cut add that erasing only the links kills 4/4 cells within 100 steps, so the ring holds the body up.

seeds_run.result: pass: ring 100% of cell-frames, 99 persistent splits, gen 18, 56 ringed swimmers >= 3 BL, 1 swim+ring+divide lineage (#372); labkit pack also seed 9
pass: ring 99.9%, 106 persistent splits, gen 16, 49 swimmers >= 3 BL, 1 swim+ring+divide lineage (#391)

controls_run.B: 20261025T2359-c29-review-ringswim-cut s7/, s8/: links-only erasure kills 4/4 cells within 60-100 steps while branched twins live (the ring does work)

verdicts.limitation: The genealogy is reticulate (merges 0.71-0.75 of splits), and swimming, ring and division co-occur in one track segment only once per seed, because tracks break at collisions. #372's second daughter swims only 0.36 BL. The drive is the per-body label average (nonlocal), as in the established SIMD claim. The ring is chi-drift adsorption of the cell's own product (L3 quasi-equilibrium clause: the cell makes all L). No dt or resolution test, and no Laplacian-only twin.
